question: Does a small replay buffer of old-class exemplars let a task-agnostic MLP keep earlier classes better than naive sequential fine-tuning on a class-incremental digits benchmark?
method: 5 class-incremental tasks (2 digit classes each), task-agnostic evaluation over 10 outputs; 80/20 stratified split; baseline MLP fine-tuned sequentially vs. same MLP with 30 replayed exemplars per old class; seeds 42-44.
metric_name: final average accuracy over all 10 classes on held-out test split
baseline: MLPClassifier (1 hidden layer, 128 units), sequentially fine-tuned on each task's data only
improved: Same MLP plus a replay buffer of 30 exemplars per previously seen class, mixed into each new task's training data
notes: Naive stand-in for the paper's hierarchical model, not its method. Hyper-parameters fixed a priori (no tuning, so no CV selection was needed). Forgetting and per-task accuracies are computed on the training split to keep the test set single-use. The improved model sees more samples per task (replay) with the same epoch count, so compute is not perfectly matched. Std is over 3 seeds (population std). Single small dataset; results are indicative only.
